statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance, with one packaging difference worth recording. The book quantifies over a GIVEN natural transformation theta and asks whether theta itself is invertible; the in-tree statement is an iff between two existential data types — 'there is an iso in [C,D]' and 'there is a componentwise-iso family that is natural'. Because both sides are Type-valued and the proof is Defined, the round trip does preserve the transformation (the ⇐ direction builds an iso whose `to` component is literally the given family, the ⇒ direction returns the components of the given iso), so nothing is lost; but the statement as written does not itself assert that correspondence, and there is no separate lemma of the form (∀ x, IsIsomorphism (transform[theta] x)) → IsIsomorphism theta in [C,D].

verifier.notes: CONFIRMED PRESENT, with the record's own caveat endorsed. Blind pass landed on the same carrier and hesitated between PRESENT and PARTIAL for exactly the reason the strength_comparison records, so the record is not overclaiming. I checked the round-trip claim in the source rather than accepting it: in the ⇒ branch of Instance/Fun.v:255 the family is built by `apply X` / `apply (X⁻¹)`, so to (iso x) IS transform[to X] x; in the ⇐ branch the two transforms are built by `apply x` on the given family, so the resulting iso's to-component is the given family componentwise. Hence for a given θ with all components invertible, one derivation step (package + reuse θ's naturality) yields θ invertible in [C,D] — no content is missing, only a named lemma. Note the in-tree right-hand side Functor_Setoid (Theory/Functor.v:148) carries a naturality side-condition in its Σ-type, which is essential and which the record does mention. See problems[] for a comment in Instance/Fun.v that states this less carefully.

#[export] Program Instance Cat_Cartesian : @Cartesian Cat := { product_obj := @Product; fork := fun _ _ _ F G => {| fobj := fun x => (F x, G x); fmap := fun _ _ f => (fmap[F] f, fmap[G] f) |}; exl := fun _ _ => {| fobj := fst; fmap := fun _ _ => fst |}; exr := fun _ _ => {| fobj := snd; fmap := fun _ _ => snd |} }. (* with eval {x y} : y^x × x ~> y := uncurry id (line 75); instantiated at Cat this is Awodey's clause (2): eps ∘ (F-bar × 1_C) = F, uniqueness of the transpose coming from exp_iso being an isomorphism *)

statement_record.book: The category Cat of small categories and functors is cartesian closed, the exponential of C and D being the functor category D^C = Fun(C,D): (1) eval : Fun(C,D) x C -> D is a functor; (2) every F : X x C -> D has a transpose F-bar : X -> Fun(C,D) with eps o (F-bar x 1_C) = F; (3) transposition is inverse to this, so for G : X -> Fun(C,D) the transpose of eps o (G x 1_C) is G again.
statement_record.intree: Cat_Closed : @Closed Cat Cat_Cartesian with exponent_obj := @Fun and exp_iso the setoid isomorphism (A × B ~{Cat}~> C) ≊ (A ~{Cat}~> [B,C]); `to` is currying (F ↦ x ↦ y ↦ F (x,y), with fmap[F](id,f) and fmap[F](f,id) as the inner functor action and the transformation components) and `from` is uncurrying with fmap (f,g) = fmap (snd f) ∘ transform[fmap[F] (fst f)]. eval and the beta law eval ∘ first (curry f) ≈ f come from Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v (eval := uncurry id, ump_exponents), and the two round trips are the iso_to_from / iso_from_to obligations, discharged as natural isomorphisms with identity components.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Two faithful-rephrasing notes: (i) 'small' is handled by universe polymorphism — Cat@{o h p} has obj := Category@{o h p} and lives one level up, so A, B, C must share a universe level rather than be 'small' in a fixed ambient set theory; per the library's design this is the standard treatment, not a weakening of content; (ii) the hom-setoid of Cat is Functor_Setoid, i.e. equality of functors IS natural isomorphism, so the transposition bijection and its round trips hold up to natural isomorphism rather than on the nose — the obligations in fact build isos with identity components, so nothing weaker than the book is proved. Awodey's clause (1), 'eval is a functor', is subsumed: eval := uncurry id is the image of the identity under `from`, hence a functor by construction, and the bifunctor-lemma route he uses is not needed.

Lemma bimap_id_right_left {F : C ∏ D ⟶ E} {w} `(f : z ~{C}~> w) `(g : x ~{D}~> y) : bimap f id ∘ bimap id g ≈ bimap f g. statement_record.book: Given categories A, B, C and maps F_0 : A_0 x B_0 -> C_0, F_1 : A_1 x B_1 -> C_1, these data constitute a functor F : A x B -> C if and only if (1) F is functorial in each argument separately and (2) F satisfies the interchange law F(A',beta) o F(alpha,B) = F(alpha,B') o F(A,beta).
statement_record.intree: Necessity is stated over a given bifunctor F : C ∏ D ⟶ E as the bimap lemmas: bimap_id_id, bimap_comp_id_left / bimap_comp_id_right (separate functoriality) and bimap_id_right_left / bimap_id_left_right (interchange). Sufficiency appears only inside Cat_Closed's exp_iso, whose `from` turns a functor A ⟶ [B, C] into a functor A ∏ B ⟶ C with fmap (f,g) := fmap (snd f) ∘ transform[fmap[F] (fst f)], i.e. F(alpha,beta) := F(A',beta) ∘ F(alpha,B); exp_iso being an isomorphism makes `to` and `from` mutually inverse, which is a bijection refining the book's iff.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker as a usable criterion, though not in mathematical content. Both directions exist, and the sufficiency construction uses exactly Awodey's defining formula. But there is no standalone lemma over RAW data (F_0, F_1) plus hypotheses (1)+(2); the hypotheses have to be pre-assembled as a functor A ⟶ [B, C] (equivalent data — the per-object functors are (1) in the second variable, the naturality of each fmap[F] f is (2), and fmap_id/fmap_comp in [B,C] are (1) in the first variable — but a different, heavier interface), and going through Cat_Closed additionally forces A, B, C to be objects of one Cat, hence to share a universe level. The library's only raw-data eliminator, Construction/Funny.v's SepFunctorial/FunnyUP, deliberately OMITS interchange and lands in the funny tensor C □ D, not in C ∏ D.
